quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move slowly until traffic ahead clears.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Do not enter the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
Honk your horn to make cars move forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side. You will block the intersection. Wait for traffic to clear so you can drive all the way through.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way, even when you signal your turn.

questions.question: When following a school bus or tank truck, you should:

options.text: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks with flammable liquids must stop at all railroad crossings. Be ready to stop when following these vehicles at railroad crossings.

questions.question: An oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer right to escape. Steering left is dangerous because the other driver might correct at the last moment and you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour slower reduces the impact.

questions.question: If your Anti-Lock Braking System vehicle loses traction on a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press hard on the brake pedal, hold it, and steer to safety. The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will pump the brakes automatically faster than you can. If you release the brake or pump it, you will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: When visibility is reduced, your first action should be to:

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you cannot see clearly. This is your first action when conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in school zones unless a different speed is posted?
questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in a school zone is 25 miles per hour. Follow any posted speed limit signs that show a different speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This is a yellow and black warning sign. It tells you a lane is ending. Be ready to merge safely with other traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: This is a yellow and black warning sign. It warns you that a sharp turn is coming. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means stop, just like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead curves right and then left. Slow down to safely drive through these curves.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand point downward. What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Left arm and hand pointing down means the driver plans to stop. If you are following this driver, be prepared to stop too.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances.
questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to places. They help you when driving in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the center line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look to the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights of an oncoming vehicle. Then look ahead again to check where the other car is.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should NOT:

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to the right exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the road or shoulder. Keep driving to the next exit. Other drivers will not expect a car backing up and will likely crash into you.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on everything EXCEPT:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your weight. It does not depend on your fitness level or how well you think you can handle alcohol.

questions.question: To turn quickly, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and allows you to turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow X on a lane control signal for a reversible lane mean?

options.text: The signal will change to a red X soon.
The signal will change to a green arrow soon.
You may only use this lane to turn.
You may drive slowly in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only use this lane to turn.
questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed and if toll booths are open. A flashing yellow X means you can only use this lane to make a left turn.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped, yellow, and have black markings. They alert drivers to unexpected road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Merge in the direction the arrow points.
Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic will stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.
